name: Inca Trail to Machu Picchu
summary: The permitted route from Km 82 up the Cusichaca valley and over three passes, the highest being Warmiwañusca at 4,215 m, entering Machu Picchu through the Sun Gate on the final morning. Roughly 43 km; permits are capped daily and sell out months ahead.

name: Short Inca Trail
summary: The last section of the Inca Trail, joined from the railway at Km 104 and walked in one day past Chachabamba and Wiñay Wayna to the Sun Gate, with a night in Aguas Calientes before the Machu Picchu visit. About 11 km, no camping, but the same permit system as the four-day route.

name: Salkantay Trek
summary: A pass route below Salkantay from Mollepata, crossing the 4,630 m Salkantay Pass and then descending through cloud forest towards Santa Teresa and Aguas Calientes. It needs no Inca Trail permit, which is why it is the usual alternative when those run out.

name: Salkantay–Inca Trail Trek
season: April – October (Inca Trail section closed all February)
summary: Approaches Salkantay from Mollepata and crosses the Incachiriasca Pass at 5,100 m, then joins the classic Inca Trail at Wayllabamba for the final stretch over Dead Woman's Pass into Machu Picchu. Higher than either route walked alone, and it still requires an Inca Trail permit.

name: Lares Trek
summary: A route through the Lares valley north of the Sacred Valley, past weaving villages and high lakes, normally finishing at Ollantaytambo for the train to Machu Picchu. Operators run several different lines through the valley: the classic one tops out at Ipsaycocha Pass, while variants cross Condor Pass nearer 4,700 m.

name: Choquequirao Trek
summary: An out-and-back from Cachora that drops about 1,500 m to the Apurímac river and climbs the same again to the Choquequirao ruins at 3,050 m, then returns the same way. The altitude is modest for the region but the ascents are long and the canyon is hot.

name: Choquequirao–Machu Picchu Trek
summary: Carries on past Choquequirao instead of turning back, crossing the Vilcabamba range by way of Yanama Pass at 4,668 m and dropping to Santa Teresa and Aguas Calientes. Around 100 km, with repeated descents to river level and climbs back out.

name: Ausangate Trek
summary: A circuit of Ausangate south-east of Cusco crossing four passes, the highest being Palomani at 5,165 m, with every camp above 4,000 m. Remote and very cold at night; acclimatisation matters more here than fitness.

name: Ausangate & Rainbow Mountain Trek
summary: The Ausangate circuit extended to take in Vinicunca, the striped ridge at about 5,036 m, reached on foot from the trek rather than on the day-trip road from Cusco. It adds a day or two to the circuit and holds the same altitude throughout.

name: Huchuy Qosqo Trek
summary: A short route from Tambomachay above Cusco over a pass of about 4,200 m and down to the Inca site of Huchuy Qosqo at 3,650 m, then on to Lamay or Calca in the Sacred Valley. Around 15 km of walking, usually sold with a train to Machu Picchu the next day.

name: Ancascocha Trek
summary: A quieter line between the Salkantay and Inca Trail routes, from Socma past Ancascocha lake and over Huayanay Pass at 4,650 m, coming out at the Km 82 railhead for the train to Machu Picchu. It needs no Inca Trail permit and sees few other walkers.

name: Vilcabamba to Machu Picchu
summary: The route from Huancacalle, beside the Inca sites of Vitcos and Ñusta Hispana, over the Choquetacarpo pass at about 4,600 m and down through Yanama and Santa Teresa to Machu Picchu. Long, remote and walked by far fewer people than the Salkantay or Inca Trail routes.
